newsitem.title: EGYPT: CIB dividend again pulls down Egypt shares.
newsitem.headline: CIB dividend again pulls down Egypt shares.

text.p: Egyptian share prices fell for the third straight trading day on Sunday in a market dominated by bank dividends and expectations of further privatisation.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) said its all-share index slipped 1.56 points to 351.52 in about average volume of 59.77 million pounds ($17.61 million).
A feature of the day was the state's sale of a majority 75 percent stake in General Upper Egypt Contracting for a total of 8.662 million pounds -- 38.50 for each of the 225,000 shares.

Commercial International Bank/CIB fell again on disappointment that it was paying a dividend of 2.00 pounds for the 1996 financial year, brokers said. The shares closed at 64.90 pounds, 2.08 pounds down on Thursday.
"People had expected a higher dividend and they started selling sraight after the general assembly on Thursday," said Ghada AlKady, strategist at Prime Investments.
Shares in Misr International Bank/MIBANK also fell, despite an increase in the 1996 dividend to 15 pounds, plus one free share for every four, from 10 pounds in 1995.
Brokers said investors had already discounted the higher dividend, which was approved by a general assembly on Saturday.
The shares closed 6.00 pounds down at 603.00.
The most active share of the day was Heliopolis Housing and Development, which ended unchanged at 395.00.

"There has been large demand since it fell under 400. People are expecting complete privatisation," said Mohamed Abdullah, a senior executive at brokers Intercapital. The state retans a 75 percent stake in Heliopolis Housing.
The index for openly traded firms fell to 483.81 points from 486.88 points on Thursday and that for the rarely-traded "closed" firms also slipped to 259.32 from 260.23.
Out of 78 shares traded, 30 rose and 28 fell while 20 ended unchanged.
